NIDDK explains that Hashimoto disease causes the immune system to produce antibodies attacking the thyroid, that white blood cells accumulate within the gland, and that thyroid tissue becomes damaged. The inflammatory component is supported by immune-cell infiltration and the identification of Hashimoto disease as autoimmune thyroiditis. This supports Autoimmune attack on the thyroid in Hashimoto disease → Inflammation and damage to thyroid tissue as CAUSES. Detailed inflammatory molecular mechanisms are not specified. source_passage_locator: K060S02: NIDDK Hashimoto's Disease → What is Hashimoto's disease? → Thyroid damage and insufficient hormone production; What are the complications of Hashimoto's disease?; What are the symptoms of Hashimoto's disease?
review_note: Reviewed K060S02 and SRC015. K060S02 directly establishes that autoimmune thyroid injury damages the gland and reduces its capacity to produce sufficient thyroid hormones, frequently resulting in hypothyroidism. This supports Inflammation and damage to thyroid tissue → Reduced thyroid hormone production (hypothyroidism) as CAUSES. SRC015 independently confirms that Hashimoto-related thyroid inflammation can impair hormone production but does not explicitly establish tissue damage in its cited passage. It remains partial for the exact composite cause node and is excluded from supporting_source_ids. Hashimoto disease may exist before hypothyroidism develops; thyroid hormone deficiency is not inevitable at every stage. AI-assisted review; human confirmation pending.
